sections.h2: Who does what with a tax bill in Russell County?
sections.html:
Four county offices share the job. The PVA, at (270) 343-4395, assigns each parcel its worth. The sheriff, at (270) 343-2191, takes the money. The clerk, at (270) 343-2125, picks up bills nobody paid in time. The county attorney, at (270) 343-2121, mails the warning letters that come before the clerk's auction of delinquent bills.

The fiscal court's page on the PVA says the office's valuations underpin the bills that finance local services. So a complaint about the number belongs with the PVA, while a question about where to send a check belongs with the sheriff.

sections.h2: What is Russell County like for a homeowner?
sections.html:
This is a lake-and-ridge county in south central Kentucky. The legislature carved it out on December 14, 1825 from parts of Adair, Cumberland and Wayne. It covers 283 square miles, with about 29 of them under water. The ground drops from 1,140 feet on Dickerson Ridge in the far north to 530 feet beside the Cumberland River. Jamestown has the courthouse. Russell Springs is the larger town, at 2,715 residents in 2020 versus 1,867. The 2020 census classed all of the county as rural.

Clocks here run on Central time, and the neighboring counties of Casey, Pulaski and Wayne to the east run on Eastern, so confirm the hour when a distant buyer or title office schedules your closing. The Cumberland Parkway passes through Russell Springs on the way to Columbia and Somerset, and US 127 ties the town to the lake and the Tennessee line.

  • Wolf Creek Dam, in the south, holds back the Cumberland River as Lake Cumberland. Water first rose behind it in 1952, and the shoreline stretches roughly 1,255 miles.
  • The Corps began lowering the lake in 2007 because of seepage under the dam. A new concrete wall inside the structure was complete by early 2013, and normal pool returned in spring 2014.
  • Summer pool normally sits near 723 feet above sea level, with the tree line a little higher.
  • A January 19, 2016 referendum ended the county's dry status, 3,833 votes to 3,423.
  • A local telephone cooperative finished a fiber network in 2015 that made Jamestown and Russell Springs early gigabit towns in Kentucky.

Russell Springs began as a resort around a mineral spring and incorporated in 1936. Jamestown incorporated in 1826 and carries the first name of landowner James Wooldridge. Lakefront sellers should expect questions about the drawdown years. The county also elects a surveyor, a useful contact when a shoreline line is in doubt.

sections.h2: How do Russell County housing numbers compare with the rest of Kentucky?
sections.html:
Homes are modest in price and the stock is loose. The 2020 census listed 10,088 housing units, and 26.0 percent stood vacant. Only 5 building permits were issued in 2025, so you are not competing with new builds. Roughly 22.6 percent of residents are past 65, and a commute averages 19.8 minutes.

With a typical value near $163,200, the yearly bill itself is rarely the obstacle in a sale. Several unpaid years on an inherited house can still eat most of the equity.

sections.h2: Why do buyers come to Russell County?
sections.html:
Mostly for the water. Among the 383 lakes run by the Corps, Lake Cumberland ranks fourth for visitor hours, and over 1,500 houseboats float on it. Lake Cumberland State Resort Park and General Burnside Island State Park both sit on its shores, and the Wolf Creek National Fish Hatchery works just below the dam, inside Russell County.

  • County median age at the 2020 census: 43.8.
  • Share of occupied homes owned by their occupants in 2020: 71.8 percent.
  • Households made up of one person living alone: 29.4 percent.

Pair that audience with a clean paper trail: a current bill, a payoff letter if needed, and a plain answer on any back years.

sections.h2: When is Russell County tax due, and how much do late payers owe?
sections.html:
One statewide schedule, from KRS 134.015, governs. Full payment by November 1 earns 2 percent off. After that the printed figure stands through December 31. A 5 percent charge arrives in January, and 10 percent from February 1.

The clerk's page says bills reach mailboxes in October and the sheriff accepts payment until April 15 of the following year. By statute the tax is a personal debt of the person who owned the property on January 1, so your sales contract should say who reimburses whom.

sections.h2: What happens if a Russell County bill is still open on April 15?
sections.html:
The sheriff passes it to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency, and a lien goes on record against the parcel. That lien survives a change of ownership. The clerk's page commits to a sale before August ends, advertised in the paper and online. Private buyers who register with the state may buy the certificate and then chase the owner for payment.

  • Amounts on the clerk's delinquent list move monthly, so ask for a fresh payoff figure.
  • The state revenue department says interest of 1 percent per month runs on the certificate, with clerk and attorney commissions on top.
  • A title search will surface the lien, so settle it ahead of closing.

sections.h2: Can I challenge what the PVA says my Russell County home is worth?
sections.html: Yes. Open with an informal conference at the PVA, which can be done by phone. If that fails, file a written petition with the clerk by the workday after the roll's inspection period ends. Bring listings, building costs or loan papers. The appeal does not freeze collection, so pay on your own claimed figure while it runs.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Russell County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Owners 65 and over, and owners classified as totally disabled. The Department of Revenue set the deduction at $49,100 for assessment years 2025 and 2026, so a county home assessed at $175,000 is taxed as if it were $125,900. With about 22.6 percent of residents past 65, many local owners will want it.

Apply at the PVA. Disability claimants must show a federal or retirement-system classification and generally renew yearly. Ask what the figure is for the current assessment year, since the state revises it.

sections.h2: What changes at the closing table for a Russell County sale?
sections.html:
Closing agents usually pull the current bill and any delinquent payoff, so ask for both early. A bill open before April 15 sits with the sheriff, and after that date it sits with the clerk, plus extra charges.

Cabins used seasonally, inherited houses and homes several years behind deserve a written payoff from the clerk before you list. A buyer who spots a lien in the title search will demand its removal or leave.

faqs.q: Where does a Russell County tax payment go?
faqs.a: To the sheriff's office, at (270) 343-2191, through April 15 of the year after the bill. After that, unpaid bills sit with the county clerk at (270) 343-2125.

faqs.q: What does a late Russell County payment cost?
faqs.a: Five percent in January and ten percent from February 1, under KRS 134.015. Once the clerk holds the bill, 1 percent monthly interest plus clerk and county attorney fees are added.

faqs.q: Will a Russell County tax lien follow a house into a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. KRS 134.015 keeps the lien on the parcel until the tax is paid or the 11-year limit in KRS 134.420 runs out, whoever owns it. A title search flags it.

faqs.q: What month does the Russell County clerk hold the tax sale?
faqs.a: Before the end of August. Newspaper and website notices go out ahead of it, and the clerk's office can confirm the date at (270) 343-2125.

faqs.q: Is the Russell County homestead exemption automatic once I turn 65?
faqs.a: No. Take proof of your age or disability status to the PVA and apply. The 2025 and 2026 amount was $49,100, and most disability claims renew every year.
